req.title: Index renders even with zero posts
req.statement: The system shall render the index page with 'No posts' or empty state when the post table is empty.
triggers: index renders even with zero posts

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-037 requires the index page to render correctly when the post table is empty. The default DB has 20 posts, so we must delete all posts before testing the empty-state. We need: (1) a positive test confirming HTTP 200 and empty-state rendering when posts are deleted, (2) a negative test confirming the index still returns 200 (not 4xx) even with no posts — verifying the error pathway is not triggered, (3) a boundary test at the exact transition from 1 post to 0 posts (last post deleted triggers empty state). We also add a state-transition test covering the normal (non-empty) index to confirm the contrast. All tests use in-process Flask test client, delete posts via direct DB manipulation inside the app context, and assert exact status codes and response body content.

tests.name: test_index_empty_posts_returns_200
preconditions: App is created with a fresh temporary SQLite database initialised via init_db()
All 20 pre-loaded posts are deleted so the post table is empty
actions: Delete all rows from the post table inside the app context
Send GET / with the test client
expected: Response body does not raise a server error
trace: R-FLASKR-037: system shall render index page with HTTP 2xx when post table is empty
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute('DELETE FROM post')
    db.commit()
    row = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()
    assert row[0] == 0

client = app.test_client()
response = client.get('/')
assert response.status_code == 200
assert response.status_code != 404
assert response.status_code != 500

tests.name: test_index_last_post_deleted_triggers_empty_state
preconditions: App is created with a fresh temporary SQLite database initialised via init_db()
Exactly 1 post remains in the post table (all others deleted)
actions: Delete 19 of the 20 pre-loaded posts leaving exactly 1
Confirm GET / returns 200 with that post's title in the body
Delete the final post so the table is empty (boundary: 1 -> 0)
Send GET / again and confirm 200 is still returned
expected: With 1 post: HTTP 200 and the remaining post title appears in the response
With 0 posts: HTTP 200 still returned (boundary at zero posts)
trace: R-FLASKR-037: boundary at exactly zero posts — transition from last post to empty table must still yield HTTP 2xx
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute('DELETE FROM post WHERE id != 20')
    db.commit()
    count = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0]
    assert count == 1

client = app.test_client()
response_one = client.get('/')
assert response_one.status_code == 200
assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in response_one.data

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    db.execute('DELETE FROM post WHERE id = 20')
    db.commit()
    count = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0]
    assert count == 0

response_zero = client.get('/')
assert response_zero.status_code == 200
assert b'Heacon signal pulse' not in response_zero.data

All posts deleted — post table has exactly 0 rows

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute('DELETE FROM post')
    db.commit()
    assert db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0] == 0

client = app.test_client()
response = client.get('/')
assert response.status_code == 200
data_lower = response.data.lower()
assert b'internal server error' not in data_lower
assert b'<html' in data_lower or b'<!doctype' in data_lower
assert len(response.data) > 10
